newsitem.title: PERU: Milpo jumps on Lima bolsa to join mining bull run.
newsitem.headline: Milpo jumps on Lima bolsa to join mining bull run.

text.p: Polymetallic miner Milpo's share price joined the mining sector's bull run Tuesday with a 7.87 percent leap by late trade due to speculative buying on the Lima Stock Exchange, brokers said.
At 11.45 a.m. local time (1645 GMT), after two hours and 45 minutes' trade in the four hour session, Milpo's price stood at 27.40 soles on volume of 51,916 shares.
"It's a good miner with interesting prospects but for the moment the moves are just because it is being led up by the rest of mining sector," said Pablo Navarro of local brokerage Fortuna.
He added the rises were due to a few investors positioning themselves in the stock hoping the sector's bull run would lift Milpo's price further and allow them to take profits.
While the mining sector has seen its liquid labor shares gain more than 125 percent since the start of the year, Milpo has not figured strongly in the record bull run.

Polymetallic miners Morococha and Atacocha have led the sector's climb this month. By late trade Tuesday, Morococha climbed 7.84 percent to 6.05 soles on volume of 62,151 shares, while Atacocha saw little trade.
The second-tier mining stock Perubar was active Tuesday, rising by late trade 10.02 percent to 6.59 soles on volume of 267,010 shares.
Perubar has a 30 percent stake in a joint venture run by Switzerland's Glencore International that exploits Peru's largest zinc mine Iscaycruz.
